🏆 Best Model

SVM-RBF with Group_B_Financial_Health feature set (21 financial ratios)

Parameters: C=10, class_weight='balanced', gamma='scale' · Threshold: 0.3721 (optimized)

The model correctly identifies 73.7% of distressed companies (class 0) while maintaining 55.3% precision — meaning when it flags a company as distressed, it's correct 55% of the time.

Key Findings

  • Financial health ratios (liquidity, leverage, cash flow) are more predictive than temporal/lag features for distress detection
  • XGBoost is the best tree-based model; SVM-RBF outperforms all others for class 0
  • Threshold tuning is critical — e.g., XGBoost default (0.5) catches only 30% of distress, but tuned threshold catches 72%
  • Industry average Z-score has been declining over recent years, with more companies entering the distress zone
  • 3-class classification achieves ~70% accuracy, but focusing on binary class 0 yields significantly better distress detection

SHAP Insights for Thesis

  • Cash flow coverage (ocf_to_finance_cost) is the single most important predictor — companies with low OCF relative to interest payments are at highest distress risk
  • Leverage (Debt_Ratio, Total_Debt_to_Total_Assets) is the second most important group — highly leveraged companies are more likely distressed
  • Industry-relative metrics matter — being below industry average on ROA, Z-score, or OCF/debt is more informative than absolute values
  • Retained earnings (X2, Retained_Earnings_to_Assets) reflects cumulative profitability — negative values strongly signal distress
  • Z-scores appear in top 20 as expected — they aggregate multiple signals into a single distress indicator

7. Methodology Notes

Data Preprocessing

  • Missing values: Median imputation (fit on training data only)
  • Feature scaling: StandardScaler (fit on training data only)
  • Class imbalance: SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Oversampling) applied only on training set — classes balanced to 692 each
  • No data leakage: Strict temporal split — train < validation < test by year

Feature Sets (from literature review)

SetDescriptionFeatures
Group_AAltman Core — Z-score components16
Group_BFinancial Health — ratios (liquidity, leverage, profitability)21
Group_CDynamic Temporal — lag & change features29
Group_DHybrid Extended — Altman + financial + industry + temporal52
Group_ETop 30 Stage 1 — selected from prior analysis28
Group_FLiterature — standard financial distress indicators26
Group_GStage 1 Selected — comprehensive set73

Models Evaluated

7 classifiers × 7 feature sets = 49 base combinations + 3 ensemble methods (soft voting, stacking, weighted averaging). Hyperparameter tuning via GridSearchCV (3-fold CV). Threshold optimization on validation set for class 0 detection.

Limitations & Future Work

  • Test set is only 2 years (261 samples) — larger test window would give more robust estimates
  • Class 0 represents ~22% of test data — still imbalanced despite SMOTE
  • Probabilities from SVM may be poorly calibrated — Platt scaling could help
  • Cross-validation with expanding window would provide more reliable temporal estimates
  • External features (macroeconomic indicators, market sentiment) could improve predictions
